A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sparse Logit Sampling study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A-L support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original language-model distillation experiments, synthetic and CIFAR-100 calibration studies, throughput measurements and downstream evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds evaluations of prior-work baseline variants and a Qwen-style student.

M1.justification: V1 Section 3.4 and v2 Section 4 describe the same importance-sampling approach, unit-temperature sampling, sparse cached targets and forward-KL distillation. V2 explains sampling and count normalization more explicitly; Appendix K pseudocode is unchanged. The Qwen experiment applies the existing method to another student configuration.

E1.justification: The synthetic tasks, CIFAR-100, web/FineWeb-Edu pretraining, Tulu instruction tuning and downstream evaluation datasets are retained. The added Qwen experiment changes the student configuration without identifying a new dataset, population or task.

E2.justification: V2 Section 6.4 and Table 11 add evaluated Raman et al. (2023) and Peng et al. (2024) variants incorporating additional training components. These include difficulty-dependent learning rates and CE loss for Raman, and softmax temperature and a CE/KD weighting schedule for Peng. Their sampling-only Top-K/Top-p counterparts were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 0.5B Qwen2.5-style student trained for 10B tokens against a CE control, plus the additional baseline configurations in Section 6.4. Existing experimental protocols and hyperparameters are retained. The Qwen teacher size is unresolved: Section 7.3 specifies LLaMA-3-8B, while Table 14's caption specifies 3B.

E4.justification: V2 adds a check of applicability to a different student architecture in Section 7.3 and a calculated storage comparison in Section 5.5. Existing calibration, gradient, temperature, teacher-adaptation, loss-function and sequence-alignment analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five generations with different seeds per instruction in Appendix E.3 and retain the same seed information in Appendix K. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty-reporting practices, confidence intervals or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Existing result values, including Appendix L, are retained. New entries include the prior-work comparisons, calculated storage requirements, and Qwen results: CE versus random sampling gives LM loss 2.99 versus 2.95 and acceptance 58.9% versus 60.0% in Table 14. New Table 11 reports -47% for Peng's sampling-only configuration, conflicting with +47% for the matching Top-p configuration in retained Table 1.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.6 derives unbiasedness of normalized sample counts at unit temperature. Appendix A.3 adds an explicit expectation-based argument for Top-K bias. The previous gradient-preservation proof is retained as A.7; the underlying loss and gradient derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: Top-K bias and inadequate tail supervision, unbiased random sampling with expected-gradient preservation, and performance near FullKD using sparse cached logits with low training overhead.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly qualifies the sampling-rounds-to-unique-tokens relationship as dataset- and teacher-dependent in Appendix C. It also asserts broader architectural applicability and interprets cited Gemma 3 results as support for larger-scale applicability. The formal Limitations section and existing instruction-tuning caveat are unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a source-code repository link on the first page and implementation descriptions for the added baseline variants. It makes the sampled-count calculation and the example of 50 draws yielding approximately 12 unique tokens explicit. Quantization details, hardware, package versions, hyperparameters and pseudocode were already supplied in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Busbridge et al. (2025), Gemma 3 by Kamath et al. (2025), and Qwen Team (2024). It identifies Gemma 3 as contemporaneous work apparently using the same sampling approach and extends the discussion of Raman and Peng with direct evaluations. Most related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 separates the earlier Proposed Methods section into Partial Empirical Solutions and a standalone Random Sampling KD section, expanding the latter into labeled explanatory steps. It also corrects numerous table references, removes the duplicated '(Copy)' artifact and clarifies student/teacher probability notation. Most prose and document organization are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 5, 11 and 14 for storage, prior-work comparisons and Qwen results. Existing tables and figures shift position with the revised text, while retaining their general presentation. All figure graphics are unchanged; Appendix L's table is retained with a new number.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity and reproducibility through the expanded method explanation, explicit unbiasedness derivation and code link. The targeted baseline, architecture and storage comparisons add useful supporting evidence. These gains are limited by conflicting reporting in the new material: Table 11's Peng percentage disagrees with Table 1, and Table 14's teacher size disagrees with Section 7.3. Overall, the revision provides a modest net improvement.
